title: Council backs GRCA stance on conservation consolidation
subtitle: Short-term rental by-law draft, Noah Road bridge land, Fergus Fall Fair fees, ice allocation, heritage grants.
overview: Council passed a resolution urging the province to meet with the Grand River Conservation Authority and seriously consider its alternative to merging conservation authorities into a large regional body {{vote:m5}}. The resolution says consolidation could weaken local governance, service delivery and fiscal accountability while municipalities fund both a regional authority and a provincial agency.

On short-term rentals, council did not adopt a by-law. It received the report, directed staff to post the draft licensing by-law on Connect CW for comment, and asked for a public meeting on related zoning changes {{vote:m7}}. Staff said licensing would start in early 2027 if council proceeds. Council also approved a discounted 2026 rate for the Fergus Fall Fair {{vote:m8}} and new ice and recreation facility allocation policies {{vote:m14}}.

After closed session, council delegated authority for road-widening land purchases and temporary construction access on two Noah Road properties for the 2026 bridge reconstruction, with a report back in open session {{vote:m4}}. The consent agenda, approved {{vote:m6}}, included an OMERS governance resolution and the acting fire chief appointment following the fire chief's retirement.

decisions.detail: Council asked the Minister and Chief Conservation Executive to meet GRCA representatives and seriously consider its alternative to consolidation, and to circulate the resolution to provincial officials and local MPPs.

decisions.item: Noah Road bridge land and access
decisions.detail: Council delegated authority to the Managing Director of Infrastructure Services to buy 5-metre road-allowance widenings at 7111 and 7112 Noah Road for $30,012.50 each, sign temporary construction access agreements, and report back in open session.
Council approved a discounted rate from the fees and charges by-law for the Fergus Agricultural Society's use of Township facilities and grounds for the 2026 fair, as a one-year transition.
Council approved the 2026 Ice Allocation Policy and Recreation Facility Allocation Policy, replacing the 2008 Indoor Facility Allocation Policy.
Council repealed By-law 2024-01 and authorized a revised grant by-law adding a larger grant for one project per year.
Council approved items 11.1 to 11.8, including a heritage designation notice, an OMERS governance resolution, an acting fire chief appointment and a Belwood Hall funding application.

debate: On the conservation authority resolution, one councillor asked to wait a couple of weeks for community feedback because the item was not on the agenda and the public had not heard of it. Others proceeded, saying council resolutions carry weight with the province.

The GRCA delegate said modernization is needed but a region spanning 81 municipalities risks diluting rural voices and watershed-based management. The delegate also raised concerns about local reserves and dam infrastructure funding, and recommended consolidation at the source protection region scale.

On short-term rentals, councillors asked how one licence per property interacts with existing multi-unit properties. Consultants explained existing uses are protected through zoning rules rather than the licensing by-law. One councillor worried about taking income away from families. Experts said they knew of no municipality phasing in licensing and warned of inequities.

On the Fergus Fall Fair, a delegate asked for stable, multi-year fees. Councillors supported the one-year discount but said the standard rental cost seemed high for volunteer groups. One councillor noted other groups had asked about fee waivers and worried about precedent. Staff said a fees study would review this.
On ice allocation, staff said arenas run near capacity and demand exceeds supply. Councillors welcomed the consultation and the higher priority for minor sports.
